hints: The order changes how long each task waits, but not the total sum of durations.
Sort tasks by duration, since short tasks finishing early keep later tasks' penalties smaller.
The reward is the sum of each deadline minus its completion time.
analogy: Do short errands first so they stop delaying every later errand.
example: Tasks (duration,deadline) (6,10),(8,15),(5,12): order 5,6,8 finishes at 5,11,19 for rewards 7, -1, -4, total 2.
algorithm: Sort by duration ascending. Accumulate elapsed duration and add deadline-elapsed after each task.
correctness: For any adjacent pair, doing the shorter task first cannot increase either completion-time sum; swapping every inverted pair yields nondecreasing duration and maximum total reward.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(1) extra space beyond sorting.
